answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nonrefundable stake before it may vote on shared tasks; rewards accrue only when independent peers attest to useful work, while proven fraud burns the stake. One person can still create many accounts, but each has to tie up real capital and risk losing it, so a sybil swarm becomes expensive rather than free. The lantern may guide a voyage across an ocean of agents, but it cannot make the toll disappear.
